key_insight: An AI agent can take an unsafe action even when the user’s request is benign and every tool-returned statement is true—if a critical safety fact is missing. EpiSEM-Bench tests how agents handle these evidence gaps.
problem_solved: Evaluating whether tool-using LLM agents respect safety boundaries and recover missing evidence before acting, rather than treating incomplete information as permission.
method: Introduce an executable benchmark with 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains.
Evaluate agent behavior when tool responses omit safety-relevant environmental facts.
Assess unsafe execution, safety-boundary adherence, and evidence recovery.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the benchmark provides a way to test safety failures caused by incomplete—not false—tool outputs. It highlights the need for agents to verify critical facts before taking consequential actions.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: benign request → incomplete tool response → agent decision → safe or unsafe action.
Side-by-side matched task cards highlighting the safety-critical fact that changes whether an action is permitted.
Benchmark overview graphic showing 300 matched task pairs across six domains.
Three evaluation icons: unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery.
paper_title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
paper_authors: Qijin Zhang, Hanzhen Wang, Yuehan Zhao, Haoyu Dai, Yao Shu
